text.p: Share analysts on Thursday were happy with Pohjola's announcement of plans to concentrate its life insurance business in the public part of the group, as this was expected to benefit shareholders.

"This is interesting because now the publicly traded part of the group will get into the fast-growing life-insurance sector whereas before it was only in non-life insurance," Elina Timonen, chief equities analyst at Merita Securities, told Reuters.
Pohjola CEO Iiro Viinanen said Pohjola's life insurance business' annual premium income of about three billion markka could triple in the next 10 years.
Goldman Sachs analyst Giovanni Govi called the announcement "very good news for the shareholders.
"Life mutuals in Finland's fast growing market need capital, and this is a simple way to arrange it," Govi said, adding that for a mutual company it would be difficult to raise capital.
But until more details are available Govi declined to estimate whether Pohjola's announcement would affect his earnings forecasts or recommendation on the company.
"I do not think that I will change them a lot," Govi said, adding that the reshuffle would have a positive impact on Pohjola's earnings in the long term.
Goldman Sachs had a "buy" recommendation for the share with a target of 142 markka before Pohjola announced the restructuring.
Aktia Bank analyst Henry Kallio said the price Pohjola is expected to pay, 400-500 million markka, for the shares and business of Salama from its associate Suomi, was not too high.
"The price cannot be considered expensive if it is at about that level," Kallio said.
Risto Murto, chief analyst at Erik Selin, said Pohjola's new group structure will benefit shareholders at the cost of policyholders.
"Pohjola's life insurance has been in a mutual insurance company, or in other words the benefits have accrued to policyholders," Murto said.
"Now...the benefit will more clearly be to the shareholder," he said, adding that the reshuffle will also clarify Pohjola's structure.
At 1640/1440 GMT, Pohjola's more liquid B share traded at 130.00 markka, up 11.70 markka or 10 percent.
